## Introduction

The `ukhsadatR` package provides easy access to UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) data via their API.

## Example

Below demonstrates how to retrieve daily reported COVID-19 cases at the national level for England:

```{r} 
library(ukhsadatR)

get_data(
  theme = "infectious_disease",
  sub_theme = "respiratory",
  topic = "COVID-19",
  geography_type = "Nation",
  geography = "England",
  metric = "COVID-19_cases_casesByDay"
) |>
  head()
```


## Wildcard example

For exploratory data analysis, you may wish to download more than one single combination.

It is good practice to preview the combinations first:
```{r}
get_combinations(
 theme = "infectious_disease",
   sub_theme = "antimicrobial_resistance",
   topic = "E-coli", geography_type = "Nation", geography = "*", metric = "*"
 )

```


## Whole sub-themes

`get_subtheme_data()` downloads every sub-theme of a theme in one call and can save one file per sub-theme. This is a large download, so it is not run here:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
get_subtheme_data(
  sub_themes = c("respiratory", "gastrointestinal"),
  out_dir = "ukhsa_data"
)
```


## Fingertips AMR local indicators

The package also wraps the UKHSA Fingertips "AMR local indicators" profile through the suggested `fingertipsR` package (`pak::pak("ropensci/fingertipsR")`). Preview the indicators, then download them:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fingertips_amr_indicators(themes = "resistance", rolling = "exclude")

res <- download_fingertips_amr(themes = "resistance", rolling = "exclude")
summarise_fingertips_coverage(res)
```

Pass `out_dir` to cache every indicator on disk so an interrupted download can be resumed by running the same call again.
